rows.name: super mushroom (item from a ? block)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 super mushroom, paused the moment it sat on top of the left ? block of the brick row (level x=336). list_sprites (paused, game_mode $0770=1) decodes a 4-entry OAM group at slots 42-45, origin (142,131) = top-left of a 16x16 metasprite, all sprite palette 6 and all behind_background=true, no flips:

- $76 (118), (+0,+0), no flips — upper-left (red cap top-left + white spot)
- $77 (119), (+8,+0), no flips — upper-right (red cap top-right + white spot)
- $78 (120), (+0,+8), no flips — lower-left (cap brim + stem)
- $79 (121), (+8,+8), no flips — lower-right (cap brim + stem)

Sprite palette 6 live = [15,22,48,39] = [$0F $16 $30 $27] (slot1 red $16 cap, slot2 white $30 spots, slot3 orange $27 stem/shading). So the mushroom is one 16x16 sprite form made of four consecutive CHR tiles $76-$79 (sprite pattern table $0000), palette 6. It emerges from the ? block and then slides right; it is drawn behind_background (attr $22 per entry). Proof: three screenshots - the block being hit from below, the red cap emerging above the block, and the full mushroom sitting on the block - plus the list_sprites block above. Reached with no reference: Mario placed under the block via RAM writes to player_x ($006D/$0086) with $0057/$0700 zeroed so he jumps straight up.
rows.why: the mushroom sits on top of the left ? block of the brick row in this screenshot; OAM $76-$79 in palette 6 render from sprite CHR as the spotted cap (top) and the stem (bottom)

rows.name: big Mario (super/fire-sized player, standing)
rows.notes:
Super Mario (the big form) in World 1-1, paused after he touched the super mushroom from the left ? block of the brick row ($0754 small flag 1->0, $0756 big flag 0->1, score +1000 to 001200). list_sprites (paused, game_mode $0770=1) decodes an 8-entry OAM group at slots 1-8, all sprite palette 4, no behind_background, origin (142,177) = top-left of a 16x32 metasprite (2 tiles wide x 4 tall), exactly twice the height of small Mario. Slots 1-8 are all drawn (no blank $FC filler, unlike the 16x32 small form which has 4 $FC fillers above the 16x16). Entries as (tile id, x/y offset from origin, flips):

- $00 (0), (+0,+0), no flips - row 1 upper-left (hat top)
- $01 (1), (+8,+0), no flips - row 1 upper-right (hat top/brim)
- $4C (76), (+0,+8), no flips - row 2 left (face/sideburn)
- $4D (77), (+8,+8), no flips - row 2 right (face/eye)
- $4A (74), (+0,+16), no flips - row 3 left (shirt/overalls)
- $4A (74), (+8,+16), flip_h (attr $40) - row 3 right, mirror of row 3 left
- $4B (75), (+0,+24), no flips - row 4 left (leg/shoe)
- $4B (75), (+8,+24), flip_h (attr $40) - row 4 right, mirror of row 4 left

So big Mario is a 16x32 metasprite made of six distinct CHR tiles ($00,$01,$4C,$4D,$4A,$4B) with the bottom two rows' right halves horizontally mirrored, all drawn from sprite pattern table $0000 in sprite palette 4 = [15,22,39,24] = [$0F $16 $27 $18] (slot1 red $16 hat/shirt, slot2 orange $27 skin, slot3 olive $18 hair/eyes/shoes). OAM slot 0 (tile $FF, (88,25), palette 7) is the invisible HUD coin sprite, not Mario. Proof: the growth-flag watch ($0754 1->0, $0756 0->1 over the 110 no-input frames) plus a screenshot of the visibly taller red-clad Mario and the list_sprites block above. Reached with no reference: small Mario positioned under the ? block via $006D/$0086 writes, jumped to spawn the mushroom, then let the mushroom bounce off the pipe back into him.
rows.why: tall Mario stands by the pipe in this screenshot (score 001200 after the mushroom); OAM $00/$01 (cap), $4C/$4D (face and arms), $4A and $4A(h) (overalls), $4B and $4B(h) (legs) render as big Mario, 16x32, palette 4

rows.name: fire flower (Fire Mario power-up from a ? block hit while big)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 fire flower, paused on top of the used left ? block of the brick row (level x≈336, screen origin (183,132)). PROOF: while big, Mario jumped into that ? block; the block became a used block and the flower rose out of it. list_sprites (paused, game_mode $0770=1) decodes a 4-entry OAM group at slots 28-31, all CHR tiles $D6/$D9 in SPRITE PATTERN TABLE $0000, all sprite palette 5 (OAM attr low bits = 1; attrs $21/$61), all behind_background = true. Origin (183,132) = top-left of a 16x16 metasprite. Entries as (tile id, x/y offset from origin, flips):
- $D6 (214), (+0,+0), no flips — upper-left (mirror half of the petal art)
- $D6 (214), (+8,+0), flip_h (attr $61) — upper-right
- $D9 (217), (+0,+8), no flips — lower-left
- $D9 (217), (+8,+8), flip_h (attr $61) — lower-right
read_tile $D6 = the flower's head: index-2 white petals around an index-3 orange centre with an index-1 green edge; read_tile $D9 = the lower half: an index-1 green stem/leaf shape. The sprite is symmetric, so only 2 distinct CHR tiles are used, each drawn once plain and once horizontally mirrored. Sprite palette 5 live = [15,26,48,39] = [$0F,$1A,$30,$27] (slot1 $1A green, slot2 $30 white, slot3 $27 orange). Confirmed by pixel: get_pixel_color on the head (187,136) = rgb(234,158,34) = $27 orange (palette-5 slot 3). OAM slot 0 (tile $FF, (88,25), palette 7) is the invisible HUD coin sprite and slots 52-57 are a left-facing Goomba. Reached by: fresh World 1-1, write $0756=1/$0754=0 so Mario is big, place him under the left ? block of the brick row at level x≈343 and jump; the mushroom block gives a fire flower instead of a mushroom. Found with no reference.
rows.why: the fire flower stands on the used block in this screenshot; OAM $D6 and $D6(h) (the flower head) over $D9 and $D9(h) (stem and leaves), palette 5, render as the flower

rows.name: Fire Mario's fireball (B-button projectile)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 fireball thrown by Fire Mario. REACH: after collecting the fire flower (player state $0756 went 1 -> 2 = Fire), press B on the ground; the ball is spawned at Mario's hand and travels right. PROOF (paused while one was in flight, game_mode $0770=1): list_sprites decodes a SINGLE 8x8 OAM entry (not a multi-tile metasprite) for the ball:
- sample A (paused right after the throw): OAM index 50, CHR tile $65 (101), screen x=226, y=200, attr $02 -> sprite palette 6, behind_background=false, flip_v=false, flip_h=false; hit-test returns an opaque pixel (pixel_value 2).
- sample B (5 frames later, same object): OAM index 32, tile $64 (100), x=246, y=191, attr $C2 -> sprite palette 6, flip_v=true, flip_h=true. So it moves ~+4 px/frame to the right, bounces in y, and its CHR tile cycles through the rotation set $64-$67 while OAM flips give the intermediate orientations.
The fireball is one tile drawn from SPRITE PATTERN TABLE $0000 in SPRITE PALETTE 6, live = [15,22,48,39] = [$0F,$16 red,$30 white,$27 orange]. read_tile $65 shows a round ball: index-1 red outline, index-3 orange body, index-2 white highlight. Confirmed by pixel: get_pixel_color on the ball (229,203) = rgb(181,49,32) = $16 red = palette-6 slot 1. Other OAM entries in the same frame: slot 0 tile $FF (invisible HUD coin, palette 7), slots 1-8 Mario in palette 4 (Fire Mario pose: tiles $00/$01/$4C/$4D/$4A/$4B), and a Goomba (tiles $70-$73) in palette 7. Found with no reference.
rows.why: Fire Mario (white and red) throws and the ball is in flight at his feet in this screenshot; a single 8x8 OAM entry, $65 then $64 (h+v flipped) five frames later, palette 6: the spinning fireball's frames
